slice: Dead-code retirement: the retired shell pieces, the duplicate Agents route, and five modules nothing called
method: grep of the whole tree (excluding desktop/node_modules/dist) for every importer; desktop patch 0034 cut from the pinned base; prepare-desktop.ts; desktop-patch-set.test.ts (rebuild from base); npm run compile-client + bundle grep; bun test apps/macos/test; bun run typecheck; tsc on the fork; check:repo; check:cursor-parity

question.asked: Do we still carry dead code - the chrome shell we no longer use, and things that conflict?
question.answer: Yes, in three shapes: modules with no production caller, a retired second agent surface for one window, and a third route to the Agents window inside the pinned desktop fork.

change.whyDead: Each was imported only by its own test file. The shell re-implements the same behaviour inline: markdown table separator rule at webview.ts:495, settings search at webview.ts:1428, artifact type filter at webview.ts:1915. They are residue of the pre-SSOT D06/D12/D13/A16 item set, which no longer appears in docs/ or backlog/.

removed: the caretComposer webview view and its caretAgents activity-bar container
the caret.agentsShell custom editor, the *.caret-shell document and openAgentsShellEditor()
the caretAgents fallback WebviewPanel and the provider's #panel field
the caret.openTask command (a duplicate of caret.showAgents: same handler, different title)
agentsWindowOpenMode() and the 'shell' destination it could return
retiredShellPieces.redirected: the three paths that used to reveal the full-page shell now call revealAgentSurface(), which focuses the surviving dock (caretComposerDock.focus)
retiredShellPieces.restrictedMode: the restricted renderer moved from caretComposer to caretComposerDock. Registering it on the retired view left the dock with no provider at all, so a restricted window could open the dock as a 'no data provider' error.
kept: apps/macos/src/webview.ts + TASK_WEBVIEW_CSS (the live IDE dock - S3 stays open)
scripts/shell-render-fixture.ts (a Bun.serve renderer for that same live shell, still the tool for the open AX/DOM parity check)

desktopRoute.removed: src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentWorkbench/ - 13 tracked files, a self-contained island whose only live effect was two command-palette entries
desktopRoute.conflict: caret.openAgentsWindow opened view id 'caretComposer', the retired webview shell, in parallel with workbench.action.openAgentsWindow (the extension's route). caret.openIde recorded a mode flag no when-clause reads: the context key caretWorkbenchShell appears in no condition anywhere in the tree.
desktopRoute.mechanism: manifest removals entry 'src/vs/workbench/contrib/agentWorkbench' + patch 0034-caret-drop-agent-workbench-shell.patch, whose only hunk drops the island's import from workbench.common.main.ts (a base file no other patch touches, so it reverse-checks normally)

verified.macTests: cd apps/macos && bun test test -> 611 pass / 0 fail (baseline before the change: 625 pass / 0 fail; the difference is the 5 deleted test files and the 4 agentsWindowOpenMode assertions)
caughtByExistingTests: command-contract + ide-native-command-ids flagged caretComposer.focus in focusDock()'s fallback loop the moment the view was deleted - the dead-id guard doing its job
ide-native-workbench flagged the declared command list and the registered views list
verified.forkTypecheck: cd desktop && npx tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck -> 0 errors
verified.bundle: cd desktop && npm run compile-client -> exit 0. Rebuilt out/vs/workbench/workbench.desktop.main.js contains 0 occurrences of caret.openAgentsWindow and 0 of caretWorkbenchShell; the compiled island directory is gone. The same grep before the change found the command in out-vscode and out-vscode-min.
verified.extensionBundle: bun run build -> 'Built Caret host and Mac extension in dist'. dist/mac-extension/out/extension.js now has 0 occurrences of agentsShell and 0 of caret.openTask, and carries caretComposerDock and revealAgentSurface (3 each). Before the rebuild the same file had 2 and 2: the compiled extension is what a personal build actually loads, so it was regenerated rather than left describing the deleted code.
verified.patchSet: apps/macos/test/desktop-patch-set.test.ts rebuilds the tree from the pinned base by applying all 32 patches in manifest order and compares every touched path byte-for-byte with the checkout -> pass, no drift
verified.repoChecks: node scripts/ci-validate.mjs -> CI-OK parents=198 ui=75 children=129 lock-shas=3 doc-links=137 md=82 evidence=81; bun scripts/cursor-parity-check.ts -> 340 keys checked, 0 mismatches
verified.guardTightened: apps/macos/test/omp-owner.test.ts: the 'no OMP launcher in the client' guard used exec[A-Za-z]*\([^)]*omp, which matches executeCommand("caretComposerDock.focus") for the 'omp' inside 'Composer'. It now requires a word boundary before omp, which still catches execFile("omp", ...) and execFileAsync(ompPath, ...) and no longer fires on workbench commands.

notVerified: No on-screen pass: the change was not driven in a running window with CDP. The extension half is covered by the suite that already models activation (ide-native-workbench, command-contract, menus-contract), and the desktop half by tsc + the rebuilt bundle grep, but nobody has clicked the Agents entry in a freshly packaged build.

out-vscode and out-vscode-min are earlier build outputs inside the pinned checkout and still hold the retired command until the next package run regenerates them (they are what `build-caret.ts --package` rewrites). No packaged Caret.app exists in dist/ - it holds brand/host/mac-extension/omp/omp-standalone - so no application bundle is stale.

Removing caret.openTask is a user-visible palette change: the entry is gone rather than renamed. Nothing in the repo (manifests, docs, tests, extension code) referenced it beyond the declaration itself.

Left alone on purpose, and worth naming so the next pass does not have to re-derive it: openCaretAgentsWindow() has no caller. setWorkbenchMode("agents", { newWindow: true }) is the only way into it and nothing calls it - the one new-window action the UI posts is open_ide_new_window, which takes the ide branch. It is a capability the extension holds but never offers (the base command behind caret.showAgents already opens the window), not residue of a retired design like the agentWorkbench island: deleting it would cascade into writeCaretAgentsWorkspace -> serializeCaretAgentsWorkspace -> CARET_AGENTS_WORKSPACE and the tests that pin the Agents workspace file, which is a decision about the workspace contract rather than a deletion of dead code.
